headline: Funding for the Lanesville/Lane's Cove National Register application, plus historic house plaques and demolition-delay listings.
summary: The agenda includes a $7,500 consultant fee for the Lanesville/Lane's Cove application and a planned Lane's Cove plaque. Other items cover historic house plaques and the 2027 preservation awards.

## DEMOLITION DELAY ORDINANCE

- Tim – creating list of historical contractors, to be posted to Google Docs under Demo-delay

## REVIEW OF HISTORIC HOUSE DATA PROJECTS (Susan/Julie)

- Gloucester housing overview
- Demo-delay list – top priority
  - *4 Major Housing Research Projects*
    1. City tax records, houses built 1900
       - 2,500 houses - add to MACRIS if built <1900, then add to Demo-delay
    2. MACRIS updates and additions; if new, add to Demo-delay
    3. Historic House Plaques – add to MACRIS, and if built <1900, then add to Demo-delay
       - All above research gets added to the Register
    4. Register of historic houses
       - Central database for the city of all historic buildings
       - Use NOBLE library network software to create an Omeka database (https://omeka.org/)
       - Will live in library's NOBLE Digital Heritage section https://digitalheritage.noblenet.org/s/gloucester/page/welcome
       - Susan & Julie created a layout; NOBLE tech person is creating test pages
- Lack of researchers – biggest challenge

- 11/2/26 Julie & Susan meeting: determined new approach to plaque application: deed search only

- No new plaque applications in November

- 34 new plaques distributed since restarting the program in Jan 2024
- 13 plaques distributed this year

    - 64 Middle St – hung 3/31/25 plaque in Oct 2026
    - 11 Pirates Lane (NSAA, Est. 1922) and (Wonson Wharf c1885 ) approved 8/31/26

- Possible new applicants/plaque orders:
  - 28 Friend St (Eben Brown, Master Mariner, R1851) approved 8/31/26 – research is done
  - 34-36 Summer St (Unitarian Parsonage, 1917-1939) approved 8/31/26 – research is done
  - 9 Hickory St (1866, not in MACRIS) application request 9/24 – research is underway

## FUNDING FOR LANESVILLE/Lane's Cove NATIONAL REGISTRY ~~DISTRICT~~ APPLICATION (Ralph)

- Intention is to ask for the 10 acres site to be on the Nat Reg of Historic Places – not be a District
  - Focus is on a smaller area of Lanesville center, which includes Lane's Cove, the Fish Shack, cemetery and a few smaller buildings surrounding that area that are publicly owned and a few privately owned
  - The fish shacks, seawall, and cemetery would qualify for grants to repair them if NR was passed.
- Ralph determining best way to get initial approval from MHC
  - Wendy suggested outlining the area on an assessors map and photographing all properties involved; comparing them with the 2016 document photos will show little to no change
- $7,500 consultant fee is anticipated coming from CPC – mid-2028 payout if applied for spring 2027
